costEstimate.description: The Kaurs are a two-income family with a disabled school-age child (Rajan) and a pre-school child (Maya). Rajan's disability extends his TFC eligibility to age 16 and doubles his annual cap to £4,000. Maya qualifies for 30 funded hours (both parents working, under £100k). The Bristol BS9 area offers a free breakfast club at Westbury-on-Trym CofE, reducing Rajan's costs compared to a paid club.

rajan.narrative: Rajan attends Westbury-on-Trym CofE Primary School (provider_12) for a free breakfast club and after-school club, plus Bristol North West Holiday Club (provider_19) for holiday cover. As a school-age child, no funded hours apply. However, his disability extends TFC eligibility from age 11 to age 16 and doubles the annual cap from £2,000 to £4,000. The free breakfast club saves £1,140 per year compared to a paid club at £6/session.

rajanTotal.disabilityNote: Rajan's disability doubles his TFC cap to £4,000/year. His actual costs (£2,968) are above the standard £2,000 cap, so the disability provision adds approximately £593.60 - £400.00 = £193.60 in additional TFC support compared to a non-disabled child capped at £2,000.

maya.narrative: Maya attends Stoke Bishop Pre-School (provider_17) for 5 morning and 3 afternoon sessions per week during term time. Both parents are working and under £100k, so the family qualifies for the 30-hour entitlement. Maya uses 24 hours per week — all within the 30-hour cap, so every hour is funded. However, the provider's effective rate (£8.67/hr) exceeds the Bristol government funding rate (£5.46/hr), creating a £3.21/hr shortfall.

familyTotal.summaryNote: Government support covers 55% of this family's childcare costs. Rajan's disability doubles his TFC cap to £4,000 — his actual costs (£2,968) exceed the standard £2,000 cap, so the disability provision provides an extra £194 in support. Maya benefits from having all 24 hours per week fully funded under the 30-hour entitlement, though the £3.21/hr shortfall between the provider rate (£8.67) and the Bristol government rate (£5.46) means the family still pays £2,928 towards her nursery fees. The family has 6 unused funded hours per week (30 entitlement - 24 used) which could cover additional sessions if needed. The free breakfast club at Westbury-on-Trym CofE saves £1,140 compared to a paid club at £6/session.
